notes: The same points on the three EuroHPC machines EuLLM runs on, with the same engine build:
LUMI-G (one GCD of an MI250X, ROCm), JUPITER Booster (one GH200, CUDA) and Leonardo
Booster (one A100 64 GB, CUDA). One device a point, so that a point fits each site's
rules (Leonardo: jobs of two hours at most, three GPUs at most) and the three compare
device for device; tokens per billed GPU-hour follow from what each site bills (LUMI an
MI250X module, two GCDs; JUPITER one GH200; Leonardo one A100).
graphs: on LUMI-G every server under continuous batching grew 1.3-2.5 GiB of VRAM an
hour with llama.cpp's HIP graphs on, until it died (c12-stability, 19-20-10-2026), and
EuLLM's ROCm builds now leave them out. CUDA builds keep CUDA graphs on: these points
run Qwen3-32B at 32 requests for 90 minutes with them on and off
(GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1), and the node's VRAM samples (vram_slopes.py) say whether
a CUDA server grows the same way. On a ROCm build without graphs both are the control.
speed: three models, one to 32 requests. docs/sites-comparison.md says how each site
runs its part and where the results go.
